findings.question: Does a global-group speaker model fail systematically on groupoid data?

ground_truth.dataset B: g_{r,q} varies by phone, with deviations zero-mean across phones

findings.control: the same comparison on group data gives 1.001, which is what Gpd's 3x parameter count buys on its own
findings.notes: Model G loses 160% held-out accuracy on groupoid data against 0% on group data. The gap is the phone-local part of the chart, and it cannot be absorbed by a per-speaker map at any sample size, because the phone deviations are constructed to average to zero across phones.
findings.error_label: excess ratio above the group-data baseline

findings.question: Does that conclusion survive changes in observation noise?
findings.control: the group world is re-fitted at every noise level as its own baseline
findings.notes: the excess ratio shrinks as noise grows: at high noise the residual is dominated by observation noise that neither model can explain, so the *ratio* compresses towards 1 even though the structural mismatch is unchanged. A ratio reported without its noise level is not interpretable.
